answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a stake locked in a bridge contract, slashed if the same operator is caught running duplicate agents. Reputation then accrues slowly, like pigment settling into cloth, so a fresh fake identity starts at the bottom while honest agents climb toward the zenith of trust. Forging a thousand credible identities would cost a thousand stakes plus months of honest work, making the attack more expensive than any profit it could extract.
